basic_identification.full_title: Solid Waste Management in Iron and Steel Plants — Guidelines (लौह और इस्पात संयंत्रों में ठोस अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन — दिशानिर्देश)
basic_identification.sector_category: Environment and Ecology / Waste Management (approved by the newly established Environment and Ecology Division Council and finalized by the Waste Management Sectional Committee, EED 08, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies comprehensive guidelines, technical criteria, and in-plant recycling or disposal practices for various solid wastes generated within integrated iron and steel plants (including blast furnace slag, steelmaking slag, mill scale, coke breeze, flue dust, gas-cleaning sludge, and spent refractory linings) to maximize resource recovery and prevent environmental contamination.

version_status_and_amendments.year_first_published: 1983 (originally published under the title 'Guidelines for utilization and disposal of solid waste from integrated steel plants')
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2026 standard (NIL on this copy).

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Quality and Operating Guidelines (Environment and Ecology / Waste Management)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 10447:2026 is an operational and management guideline standard rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its structured waste segregation, recycling limits, and slag-utilization criteria is legally audited by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) under national Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, and Hazardous Waste Rules. It is a mandatory component of Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and Consent to Operate (CTO) approvals for metallurgical facilities across India.

requirements.detail: Requires steel plants to establish comprehensive mapping and monthly tracking of solid wastes. Technical profiles are typically structured around a nominal baseline of a 2 Million Tonne Crude Steel per annum plant capacity to trace generation rates.

requirements.requirement_type: Segregated Sinter and Blast Furnace Feed
requirements.detail: Mill scale must be segregated by size and reutilized directly in-plant: fine mill scale (-10 mm) is routed as direct feed to the sinter plant, medium-size scale (+6 mm) is recycled through open hearth furnaces or pelletizing mixes (up to 5 percent to increase compressive pellet strength), and coarse scale (+10 mm) is reutilized as blast furnace feed.

LD/BOF steelmaking slag (typically generated at 120 kg to 220 kg per tonne of crude steel) can be reutilized as a source of flux in the blast furnace or sinter base-mix. However, the standard specifies a strict maximum recycling limit of 30 kg to 35 kg of BOF slag per tonne of sinter mix, as high phosphorus and sulfur contents in the slag can affect metallurgical quality if exceeded.

Due to its high calcium oxide (CaO = 30 to 52 percent) and magnesium oxide (MgO = 6 to 15 percent) content, BOF slag is approved for use as a soil conditioner to neutralize highly acidic agricultural soils.
Granulated blast furnace slag must be recovered and utilized to the maximum extent possible as a pozzolanic raw material for manufacturing Portland Slag Cement (PSC) to divert waste from slag dumps.

Air-cooled blast furnace slag is approved for physical infrastructure reuse, including road construction aggregates, railway ballast, or as a raw feed to manufacture insulating slag wool in accordance with IS 3677.

Coke breeze (screened out below 10 mm) and coal dust fines must be captured and reutilized as alternative fuels in sintering strands or pulverized coal injection (PCI) boilers to maximize thermal recovery.

Heavy-metal-bearing flue dust and gas-cleaning sludge containing volatile zinc, lead, or alkali compounds must be treated to recover metals, recycled under restricted ratios, or safely encapsulated and disposed of in secure landfills (SLFs) lined with geomembranes to prevent leaching.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10447 : 2026 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for the utilization and disposal of solid wastes generated within integrated iron and steel plants. Developed under the Waste Management Sectional Committee (EED 08), this updated standard provides a highly structured engineering guide to classify, recycle, and safely dispose of millions of tonnes of industrial residues like blast furnace slag, steelmaking (LD) slag, mill scale, coke breeze, and flue dusts. It outlines precise in-plant recycling limits (such as restricting BOF slag additions to 30–35 kg per tonne of sinter mix to avoid phosphorus buildup), mandates granulated slag reclamation for cement making, and details how coarse mill scale can increase the compressive strength of pellets or feed blast furnaces. This guidelines standard supports circular economy, carbon reduction, and zero-waste-to-landfill initiatives in India's steel sector.
